findings.reason: a zero after-rate from a scan that reads no death records is indistinguishable from a real zero, and that is the section's entire deliverable.
findings.text: §10's done-when states the window count, death count, rate with interval and the compared before-rate, and its only guard is the "fewer than 60 reviews" clause; nothing requires the scan to find a death known present, and §10 is the one section whose headline result is a rate that may legitimately be zero.

findings.reason: one verdict cannot close both, and the prevention half's scope is set by the demonstration's outcome, so a node dispatched to §9 has no bounded deliverable to be closed against.
findings.text: §9 delivers two things: a dispatch that demonstrates compaction and an open-ended prevention programme ("Each prevention is measured by the death rate of its cell before and after"), whose candidates and count are not fixed by the plan.
